fallacies.explanation: Mendicino stated that the work has already started and they want to get the office up and running 'as soon as possible' without offering any specifics on a timeline.
Mendicino claimed the office's launch is contingent on Parliament passing the budget bill without providing evidence or specific reasons why this is the case.
When asked about the foreign-interference office, Mendicino talked about other actions his government has pledged to pursue, which diverts attention from the specific question about the timeline.

Mendicino emphasized the $56 million earmarked in the budget for measures to combat foreign interference, but did not address the specific concerns about the delay in launching the office or the action plan.

Mendicino claimed that some in diaspora communities have avoided taking part out of concern of 'being targeted,' which evokes emotional concerns without addressing the specifics of the registry's implementation.

Mendicino shifted the focus to the complexities of creating a registry and concerns about stigmatization, sidetracking from the central issue of the delay in launching the foreign-interference office.
